items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: The Martel band... Old man Martel was the leader of the band... I don't think he ever wrote anything for Dayton... I think he would write the chords down for Hillary... But Old Man Martel was a good musician... The first time I ever played 'Sand' in my life was with him.

ctx.x: Joe Darensbourg, Tape 2, April 18, 1984. You were telling me about Martel...

The Martel band. You were asking me how I happened to start with that band. It just came to me... Martel was a family band. It was all family members. The girl, a banjo player... She played banjo. They had two banjos. One of the boys, Dayton Martel, played the trombone, and Berton Martel played the trumpet or cornet or whatever you call it, Millard Martel played drums, and they didn't have a piano. Old man Martel was the leader of the band, although Bert played...his son played trumpet. He played a little B-flat…
What was his first name? Do you remember?

items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: Now I'm talking about the Martel girl.

ctx.x: Well, she never traveled with me. Now I'm talking about the Martel girl.
